points.description: States that a stack is a data structure (or collection/container) used to store elements/items. Accept equivalent wording such as 'a structure for holding data'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it only identifies a stack as a data structure/collection but does not say it stores or holds elements.

levels.says: Only says it is a data structure/collection, without saying it stores or holds elements.

points.description: States the last-in-first-out property: the last item added is the first to be removed, or equivalently LIFO / items are removed in reverse order of insertion.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it only says items are added and removed at the same end/top, without clearly stating that the last added is first removed.

levels.says: Only says items are added/removed at one end (the top), without stating that the last added is first removed.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both parts: a stack is a data structure that stores elements, and it has last-in-first-out behaviour. Part marks are available for giving only one component or for a vague statement about adding/removing at the top. No marks are earned for an unrelated structure or for describing first-in-first-out behaviour.
